preconditions.description: The input sequence length n is a positive integer between 2 and 30000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) and -10**8 <= x <= 10**8 for x in sequence)
preconditions.description: Each element in the sequence is a distinct integer within the range [-10^8, 10^8].
All elements in the sequence are distinct.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'No solution' or (len(progression1) >= 1 and len(progression2) >= 1 and set(progression1).isdisjoint(set(progression2)) and set(progression1).union(set(progression2)) == set(sequence))
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, stdout contains exactly two non-empty arithmetic progressions (progression1 and progression2) that partition the input sequence without changing the relative order of elements. If no solution exists, stdout is exactly 'No solution'.

postconditions.expression: all(abs(progression1[i+1] - progression1[i]) == abs(progression1[1] - progression1[0]) for i in range(len(progression1)-1)) if len(progression1) > 1 else True
postconditions.description: The first progression (progression1) is an arithmetic progression, meaning the difference between consecutive elements is constant (if length > 1).

postconditions.expression: all(abs(progression2[i+1] - progression2[i]) == abs(progression2[1] - progression2[0]) for i in range(len(progression2)-1)) if len(progression2) > 1 else True
postconditions.description: The second progression (progression2) is an arithmetic progression, meaning the difference between consecutive elements is constant (if length > 1).

postconditions.expression: all(progression1[i] < progression1[i+1] or progression1[i] > progression1[i+1] for i in range(len(progression1)-1)) or len(progression1) == 1
postconditions.description: The first progression (progression1) maintains the relative order of elements from the original sequence (if length > 1).

postconditions.expression: all(progression2[i] < progression2[i+1] or progression2[i] > progression2[i+1] for i in range(len(progression2)-1)) or len(progression2) == 1
postconditions.description: The second progression (progression2) maintains the relative order of elements from the original sequence (if length > 1).
